answer: Cross-epoch behavioural fingerprinting requires each identity to reproduce its prior interaction signature across distant epochs. Agents score consistency between short-window and long-window histories, and identities whose divergence exceeds the ocean of normal drift get throttled. A sybil farm must therefore sustain coherent behaviour past the lagoon of first contact, which means paying ongoing operational cost per identity across every epoch. Divergence near the horizon of the scoring window triggers review, so attackers pay both creation and sustained maintenance to stay invisible.
